title: The fastest this design can be clocked

prereqs.why: The sum you have to build is exactly the setup-time inequality from a timing report.
Each term in the sum belongs to a different piece of the fabric — the flop, the logic, the routing, the clock tree.

statement:
A design's worst path runs from one flip-flop, through combinational logic and routing, to the next flip-flop. After place and route, the tool reports:

| Contribution | Delay |
| --- | --- |
| Clock-to-output of the source flip-flop (`t_co`) | 0.90 ns |
| Combinational logic and routing along the path | 6.20 ns |
| Setup time required at the destination flip-flop (`t_su`) | 0.35 ns |
| Worst-case clock skew between the two flops | 0.25 ns |

**What is the highest frequency this design can be clocked at, in MHz?**

Assume the skew works against you — the destination's clock arrives early, so it has less time to wait.
hints: Add up everything that must fit inside one clock period. All four rows contribute; the question is only whether skew adds or subtracts, and the problem tells you.
That sum is the minimum clock period. Frequency is one divided by the period — watch the units, since nanoseconds give gigahertz.
1 / 7.7 ns. A period in nanoseconds inverts to GHz, so multiply by 1000 to get MHz.

payload.hintFormat: A frequency in MHz, to about the nearest MHz.
